record.paper: On the clique number of random Cayley graphs and related topics

dossier_meta.paper: On the clique number of random Cayley graphs and related topics
dossier_meta.statement_text: There exists $C>0$ and a two-coloring of $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}\setminus\{0\}$ such that there is no subspace $H$ of size $Cn$ for which all nonzero elements of the subspace are monochromatic.
dossier_meta.context_text: Alon's conjecture remains wide open for $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}$ and $\mathbb{F}_{3}^{n}$. The finite unions theorem rules out a two-coloring with no monochromatic subspace at all over $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}$ for large $n$, so progress requires understanding the quantitative threshold. Establishing this conjecture would be an important step toward proving Alon's conjecture for $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}$, though the true bound on the minimum monochromatic subspace size may be considerably smaller.
